prerequisites: General knowledge of physics, chemistry and mathematics
Having taken the course Materials Science

learning_outcomes.text: Students are expected to acquire knowledge and skills in Materials Engineering in the field of Mechanics.
Know the different mechanical properties and how to obtain them from mechanical tests.
Understand the obtaining of different microstructures through phase diagrams and heat treatments.
Comprehend the internal structure of materials (metals, ceramics, and polymers) and their relationship with mechanical properties.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technique.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: Mechanical properties of materials. Mechanical tests.
BLOCK II: Microstructure control. Phase equilibrium diagrams. Heat treatments.
BLOCK III: Structure, properties and selection of metallic, ceramic and polymeric materials.
Laboratory practices: Microstructural and fractographic analysis.
teaching_methods: Lectures: master class used to present theoretical concepts of the course.
Practical classes: formulation, analysis and resolution of problems or exercises related to the course topic.
Laboratory practices: practical exercises in the laboratory.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment test (first part of the course)
Final exam (second part of the course)

assessment_rules: For the first call, the total minimum grade to pass is 5 points. The continuous assessment test and the final exam each require a minimum of 4 out of 10 points. If a part is passed, its grade can be carried over to the second call. In the second call, the final exam accounts for 80% of the grade, with a minimum of 4 out of 10 points required in each of its parts; grades from tasks and lab practices are carried over from the first call.
